name: How does building a tiny home compare to a traditional home addition?

mainEntity.name: How does building a tiny home compare to a traditional home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Building a separate backyard tiny home often offers greater flexibility and can be less disruptive than a traditional home addition. Additions typically involve modifying existing structures, which can be complex and impact the main home's living space during construction. Tiny homes, being detached, provide a completely independent unit with its own entrance, offering more privacy and rental income potential. While both increase living space and property value, ADUs are often a more streamlined construction process and can provide distinct dwelling separation, appealing to a wider range of uses.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tiny home offers independent living space, potentially less disruption, and more privacy than a traditional home addition. It provides a separate dwelling unit with its own entrance.
